title: Impact of Anterior Load Carriage on Gait in Individuals With Transfemoral Amputation
official: Impact of Anterior Load Carriage on Gait in Individuals With Transfemoral Amputation Using a Prosthesis: A Monocentric Cross-Over Study
summary: This monocentric prospective crossover study aims to evaluate the impact of anterior load carriage on gait performance in individuals with unilateral transfemoral amputation using a prosthesis. Participants will complete three randomized walking conditions during a single assessment session: no load, a light anterior load corresponding to 7.5% of body weight simulating child carrying, and a heavier anterior load corresponding to 15% of body weight simulating a utility load. Gait performance, biomechanical adaptations, physiological cost of walking, perceived exertion, and prosthetic comfort will be assessed using instrumented gait analysis and standardized clinical measures. The study seeks to improve understanding of how daily load-carrying tasks affect mobility and balance in prosthetic users and to provide evidence for rehabilitation strategies and prosthetic management.
conditions: Unilateral Transfemoral Amputation in Prosthetic Users
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 years or older.
* Unilateral transfemoral amputation.
* Regular use of a lower-limb prosthesis for at least 6 months.
* Functional level K2, K3, or K4.
* Ability to walk independently with the prosthesis, without an assistive device, and complete the study assessments.
* Stable clinical condition at the time of inclusion.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unstable residual-limb pain, socket-related pain, or musculoskeletal pain affecting gait.
* Active skin lesion or wound on the residual limb.
* Neurological, vestibular, or orthopedic disorder significantly affecting gait or balance.
* Unstable cardiovascular, respiratory, or metabolic disease contraindicating walking exercise.
* Known pregnancy.
* Persons deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision.
* Persons under legal protection incompatible with participation in the research.
